question: In which state of India is shifting cultivation known as Pamlou?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipur **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Shifting cultivation, also known as slash-and-burn agriculture, is a traditional agricultural practice.
 
• It involves clearing a patch of forest land by cutting down trees and burning the vegetation.
 
• The cleared land is then used for cultivation for a few years until the soil fertility declines.
 
• After that, the land is left fallow, allowing the forest to regenerate.
 
• This practice is common in many parts of the world, particularly in tropical regions.
 
• In India, shifting cultivation is prevalent in the northeastern states.
 
• Manipur, one of the northeastern states, has its own local name for this practice, which is Pamlou.
 
• Pamlou is a traditional agricultural practice that has been followed by various tribal communities in Manipur for generations.
 
• It is deeply rooted in the cultural and socio-economic fabric of these communities.
 
• The practice is often associated with the jhum cycle, which refers to the period of cultivation and fallow.
 
• The jhum cycle varies depending on the region and the soil fertility.
 
• Concerns about deforestation and environmental degradation have led to efforts to promote sustainable alternatives to Pamlou.
 
• Government initiatives and non-governmental organizations are working to introduce improved agricultural practices.
 
• These initiatives aim to reduce the reliance on shifting cultivation and promote sustainable land management.
 
• The terrain of Manipur, being hilly, makes this type of cultivation common.
 
• The local tribes have developed unique methods of cultivation to suit their environment.
 
• The impact of Pamlou on the environment is a topic of ongoing discussion.
 
• The practice is also tied to the social structure of the local people.
 
• Modern agricultural techniques are slowly being introduced to the region.
 
• The government is working to provide better farming methods to the local people.
